title: The Verb Sum
subtitle: sum, es, est, sumus, estis, sunt. The most common verb, irregular, mandatory.
objectives: Conjugate sum in all six persons of the present indicative.
Translate sentences using sum as a linking verb.
Understand that sum takes nominative complements, not accusative.
Recognize sum as the auxiliary for perfect passive forms.

sections.heading: The verb to be
sections.body:
sum (to be) is irregular. Learn it by heart:

Present indicative:
  sum — I am
  es — you (sg.) are
  est — he/she/it is
  sumus — we are
  estis — you (pl.) are
  sunt — they are

sum takes nominative complements:
  vir fortis est. — The man is brave. (fortis is nominative, agreeing with vir)
  puellae bonae sunt. — The girls are good.

Cicero writes: cōnsul sum. — I am consul.
Caesar writes: Helvētiī sunt fortissimī. — The Helvetians are very brave.

items.answer: sum, es, est, sumus, estis, sunt

items.prompt: What case does sum take as its complement?
